Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by D. L. Crawford.

I

At about 8.50 a.m. on January 6, 1940, an unsuccessful attempt was made on the life of Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, on Avenue Haig about 100 yards west of Route Ferguson, while he was proceeding in his motor car on the way from his home at 633 Avenue Haig to the S.M.C. Offices.

Discreet enquiries show that the crime was instigated by Wang Ching Wei's party and the Japanese Military Police with the following object in view:-

1. To frustrate the conclusion of an agreement between Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips and "Mayor" Fu Siao-en over the administration of the extra-Settlement roads area in the Western District.

2. To bring about the eventual resignation of Fu Siao-en and the appointment of Chu Ming Nyi (褚民谊), Wang Ching Wei's Secretary, to the post of "Mayor of Shanghai."

The Japanese Authorities, it is said, have altered their views towards the proposed agreement and intend to revise the terms of same. They also intend to give Chu Ming Nyi, the proposed "Mayor," instead of Fu Siao-en, the credit for the conclusion of the said agreement.

1940 年 1 月 6 日上午 8 点 50 分左右，上海公共租界工部局秘书长兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生在乘汽车从海格路 633 号家中前往工部局办公室途中，在海格路弗格森路以西约 100 码处遭遇未遂刺杀。

经 discreet 查询显示，该罪行由汪精卫派系和日本宪兵队唆使，目的如下：-

1. 阻挠 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生与“市长”傅筱庵就西区越界筑路区域的管理达成协议。

2. 促成傅筱庵最终辞职，并任命汪精卫的秘书褚民谊担任“上海市长”。

据说，日本当局已改变对拟议协议的看法，并打算修订协议条款。他们还打算让拟任“市长”褚民谊，而非傅筱庵，获得签署上述协议的功劳。

（左侧手写批注：FILE / Burnt unframed / rubbishly / M）

Chang Fu-keng (張富賡), Manager of
the Tung Tai (同泰) Compradore's Shop, 1211
Bubbling Well Road visited S.M.P. Headquarters on
the evening of 8/1/40 and gave the following
explanations regarding his conversation with Mr.
H.M. Cumine: Chang stated that at about 9. p.m.
a few days before Christmas, he was walking in a
westerly direction along Bubbling Well Road when
he overheard two male Chinese discussing the
abduction of a Mr. Phillips. He thought no more
of the matter until a day or two later when he read
an account in a Chinese newspaper which referred to
the departure from Shanghai of Sir Herbert Phillips,
H.M. Consul General. Shortly after he, Chang,
read this account Mr. Cumine came into his shop
and as he was an old customer with whom he was in
the habit of conversing, he told him about the
conversation he had overheard concerning the
abduction of a Mr. Phillips.

Beyond stating that they were dressed
in Chinese clothes, Chang is unable to give a des-
cription of the men referred to above. That they
were discussing an attempt on the life of Mr. Godfrey
Phillips is not clear, but whether or not this is so,
there seems little likelihood of Chang being able
to throw further light on the matter.

The attempted assassination of Mr. COLBY PHILLIPS
was carried out by five members of the Chinese Special
Service Corps (特務隊) which operates under the
control of the Japanese Special Service Section. This
corps was originally organized by Wang Ching Wei's
followers and they were responsible for numerous assassi-
nations in both the Settlement and the French Concession.
Recently however they were removed from the control of
Wang Ching Wei and now operate under the orders of the
Japanese Special Service Section.

In addition to the three men disguised as ricksha
coolies two others in ordinary coolie clothes were stand-
ing by, one at the gate of the " Clover Garden " and the
other at the entrance of the small lane leading to the
" Sun Sun " gambling and narcotic den. Immediately after
the shooting all five made for the lane and the three
disguised ricksha coolies tried to take off their coats
and pants. The armed guards of the " Sun Sun " did not
hear the shooting but noticed the five men hurrying towards
them. They stopped just before the main entrance to the
building and turned into an adjacent lot where they started
to take off their clothes.. Attracted by their unusual
behaviour one of the guards known as " Small Shantung "
(小山東) left his post to look things over and to
his surprise noticed that all of them were armed and the
gun of one of them was lying on the ground. His first
thought was that these men were going to hold up the " Sun
Sun " and he ran back to summon his fellow guards. When
they returned the three were still changing their clothes
and when they were surrounded by the guards one of them
shouted in " We are from the same family " ( i.e., they
were " comrades "). To the guards' questions they replied
that if they would call up the Chinese Special Service Corps

对COLBY PHILLIPS先生的暗杀未遂行动是由中国特别服务队（特務隊）的五名成员实施的，该队在日军特别服务科的指挥下运作。该队最初由汪精卫的追随者组织，他们对租界和法租界内的多起暗杀事件负责。然而，最近他们脱离了汪精卫的控制，现在根据日军特别服务科的命令行动。

除了三名伪装成人力车夫的男子外，另有两名身穿普通苦力服装的人在旁接应，一人站在“丁香花园”门口，另一人站在通往“新新”赌毒窝的小弄堂入口处。枪响后，五人立即冲向弄堂，三名伪装成人力车夫的试图脱掉外套和裤子。“新新”的武装守卫没有听到枪声，但注意到这五人匆忙向他们跑来。他们在建筑物正门前停下，转入相邻的一块空地，开始脱衣服。一名被称为“小山东”的守卫被他们的异常行为吸引，离开岗位去查看情况，惊讶地发现他们都持有武器，其中一人的枪掉在地上。他的第一反应是这些人要抢劫“新新”，于是跑回去召集其他守卫。当他们返回时，那三人仍在换衣服，当被守卫包围时，其中一人大喊“我们是一家人”（即他们是“同志”）。面对守卫的质问，他们回答说，如果守卫能呼叫中国特别服务队

pages.en:
-2-

Headquarters everything would be cleared up, they also
said that they would surrender to the guards and their
guns were duly handed over. In the meanwhile eye witnesses
of the shooting outside the line had arrived at the "Sun Sun"
and told what had happened and "Small Sha tung" himself
went to the manager of the "Sun Sun" and reported the matter.
He was told to telephone to the headquarters of the corps
immediately and when he did so he was informed that someone
would be sent over at once but under no circumstances should
the men be handed over to any other party. At the same time
the manager telephoned to Japanese Gendarmerie headquarters
in Jessfield Road and was informed that they had no interest
in the matter and that the caller should deal with the
Special Service Corps.

During the excitement the two armed men in ordinary
coolie clothes had slipped away but the other three were kept
in the Guards' quarters at the "Sun Sun" until the arrival of
five men in a car from the corps headquarters, one of them
being a detective officer of the City Government Police. They
immediately took charge of the three men and removed them in the
car.

Conversations between the guards and the three men
indicated that the shooting was the result of dissatisfaction
of the Special Service Corps over the attitude of the S.M.C.
in its dealings with the City Government and that the object
was to warn the British members of the Council by an attack on
one of the Council's leading officials. According to the
guards they could have easily killed Mr. Phillips but on
the evening before the attack final instructions had been
received from the Japanese Special Service Section that he
was not to be killed. The Japanese Naval, Military and
Gendarme authorities were alleged to have been fully aware
of the plans as opposed to the Japanese Civil authorities
pages.zh:
-2-

总部方面表示一切都会澄清，他们还称将向卫兵投降，其枪支也已按规定上交。与此同时，防线外枪击事件的目击者抵达“新新”（Sun Sun），讲述了事发经过，“小山东”（Small Sha tung）本人也前往“新新”经理处报告此事。他被告知立即致电该部队总部，当他照办时，对方告知将立即派人前来，但绝不可将这些人移交给任何其他方。同时，经理致电位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的日本宪兵队总部，得知日方对此事不感兴趣，来电者应自行与特别服务队（Special Service Corps）交涉。

在混乱中，两名身穿普通苦力服装的持枪男子溜走，但另外三人被留在“新新”的卫兵室，直到五名乘汽车从部队总部赶来的人到达，其中一人是市政府警察局的侦探官。他们立即接管了这三名男子，并用汽车将其带走。

卫兵与这三名男子的谈话表明，枪击事件是由于特别服务队对工部局（S.M.C.）在与市政府打交道时的态度感到不满所致，其目的是通过袭击市议会的一名主要官员来警告英籍议员。据卫兵称，他们本可以轻易杀死菲利普斯先生（Mr. Phillips），但在袭击前夜，他们收到了日本特别服务科（Japanese Special Service Section）的最终指令，规定不得将其杀害。据称，日本海军、陆军和宪兵当局完全知晓该计划，这与日本民政当局

pages.en:
-3-

who knew nothing before the attempt and know nothing now.

The five men who took part were once members of the
City Government Police Corps, two being from Anwei, one from
Hupeh and two from Kingpo.

Not long after the men had been taken away, Chief Officer
Wong of the City Government Police called on the management of
the "Sun Sun" accompanied by Japanese in plain clothes and the
manager and his staff were instructed to keep their mouths tight
shut. In the afternoon "Small Shantung" was summoned to the
Special Service Corps Headquarters where he was politely treated
but was warned not to mention to anyone what had actually taken
place.

形成对比，后者在企图行动之前一无所知，现在也仍不知情。

参与此事的五人曾是市政府警察部队成员，其中两人来自安徽，一人来自湖北，两人来自宁波（Kingpo）。

在这几人被带走后不久，市政府警察局的黄警官（Chief Officer Wong）在几名便衣日本人的陪同下拜访了“新新”的管理层，经理及其员工被指示严守秘密。下午，“小山东”被传唤至特别服务队总部，虽然受到礼貌对待，但被警告不得向任何人提及实际发生的情况。

Date Jan. 7th. 19 40.

Subject Attempted assassination of Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips on Avenue Haig.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With regarding to the attempted assassination of Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips on Avenue Haig at about 9 a.m. January 6, 1940, it is reported that there were altogether three assailants who opened fire on the motor car of Mr. Phillips. After the shooting, they escaped into an alley leading to Tsu Ka So, off Avenue Haig, C.O.L., but were halted by some of the armed guards of the Sun Sun Gambling Den, No. 30 Tsu Ka So, in front of the den owing to the fact that they were holding pistols in their hands and were therefore suspected of being armed robbers. They told the armed guards of the gambling den that they belonged to "Kung Kwan" ("Residence", indicating 76 Jessfield Road, the Headquarters of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army) and were taken to No. 7 Mei Hwa Li, Tsu Ka So, off Edinburgh Road and Avenue Haig, where a section of the Special Service Corps is located. They were transported to 76 Jessfield Road and later handed over to Japanese Gendarmerie.

According to an unconfirmed report, the attempted assassination was carried out by members of the China Peace National Salvation Alliance Army which has an office at 76 Jessfield Road and which is organizing an anti-White people movement. 主题：海格路（Avenue Haig）戈弗雷·菲利普斯先生（Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips）遇刺未遂案。

由副督察廖仲坚（D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien）呈报，经督察克劳福德（D.I. Crawford）转呈

关于1940年1月6日上午9时许在海格路发生的戈弗雷·菲利普斯先生遇刺未遂案，据报共有三名袭击者向菲利普斯先生的汽车开枪。枪击后，他们逃入海格路旁通往曹家渡（Tsu Ka So）的一条弄堂，但因手持手枪，被怀疑为武装劫匪，而在曹家渡30号“新新”赌窟门前被该赌窟的部分武装卫兵拦下。他们告诉赌窟的武装卫兵，他们属于“公馆”（Kung Kwan，即“住所”，指极司菲尔路76号，中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队总部），随后被带至爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）和海格路旁曹家渡梅花里7号，那里驻有特别服务队的一个分队。他们随后被送往极司菲尔路76号，之后移交给日本宪兵队。

据未经证实的消息称，此次刺杀企图是由“中华和平救国联盟军”（China Peace National Salvation Alliance Army）成员实施的，该组织在极司菲尔路76号设有办事处，并正在组织一场反白人运动。兹回顾，1月4日上午，彩色纸质海报

Captain of a special service corps, dispatched two of
his followers named YUE KOH TAI (俞國泰) and TS
TSUNG LOONG (朱振隆) with two others, all armed with

R.T. Tabrum
D.I.

P.S.
The attempted assassins are natives of Anwhei.

R.T.T.

doubt be known to our Special Branch. The informant specially
requests that this information be not typewritten. C.I.
MacFarlane informs me that the Japanese Gendarmerie have
visited S.C.C. Police Headquarters and severely censured those
Officers who imparted the information in re "arrests" to the
S.M.P.

R.T. Tabrum
D. I.

此信息立即转告史密斯巡官，后者将其转达给麦克法兰首席巡官和塔布鲁姆探长，再由后者转告“B”区警务督察约克先生，约克先生指示麦克法兰首席巡官去会见上海市政府警察局极司菲尔路11/13号的王德林（Wang Teh Ling）警监。
麦克法兰首席巡官走访了该地址并会见了上述警监，在向其通报了工部局警务处掌握的关于这些逮捕行动的信息后，该警监打了几通电话，然后告知麦克法兰首席巡官，这三名男子是由中国国民党反共救国军特务队成员逮捕的，该机构在朱家

pages.en:
- 4 -
Soo Village. (The Headquarters of this organization is
located at 76 Jessfield Road).

Superintendent Wong added that there was every
likelihood of the arrested persons being handed over
to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters at 94 Jessfield
Road.

Superintendent Wong having nothing further to impart
C.I. MacFarlane telephoned to Mr. Yorke, D.O. "B" Div.
apprising him of what he had learned and Mr. Yorke
instructed him to return to the station.

At 9.45a.m. 6/1/40, two public ricksha coolies by
name Chi Ts Hong (李志洪) and Zan Tsung Yei (曹振賢)
came to the station, followed at 11a.m. 6/1/40, by
another named Wang Ho Foo (王合福).

They reported that they were plying their several
rickshas at different places in the western area at about
6 a.m. when each was approached by a male Chinese who
asked to be pulled to a lane on Jessfield Road opposite
the Yeong Ching Li (榮慶里). On arrival there the
three coolies were compelled to divest themselves of
their ricksha pullers smocks and other articles of
clothing by a number of armed men.

They were then taken to a nearby teashop and kept
there, guarded by two men armed with Mauser pistols
until after 9a.m., when they were told they could go,
and that their rickshas had been left at a piece of waste
ground off Brenan Road.

Subsequent to their release they went to the waste
pages.zh:
- 4 -
厙村设有一个分站。（该组织的总部设在极司菲尔路76号）。

王警监补充说，被捕人员极有可能被移交给设在极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队总部。

鉴于王警监没有更多情报提供，麦克法兰首席巡官致电“B”区警务督察约克先生，告知其所获情况，约克先生指示他返回捕房。

1940年1月6日上午9时45分，两名名为李志洪（Chi Ts Hong）和曹振贤（Zan Tsung Yei）的公共人力车夫来到捕房，随后在1940年1月6日上午11时，另一名名为王合福（Wang Ho Foo）的车夫也来到捕房。

他们报告称，早上6点左右，他们各自在西区不同地点拉车时，分别有一名中国男子上前要求拉到极司菲尔路荣庆里（Yeong Ching Li）对面的一条弄堂。到达那里后，这三名车夫被数名武装人员强迫脱下人力车夫的罩衫和其他衣物。

随后他们被带到附近的一家茶馆，由两名持有毛瑟手枪的人看守，直到上午9点过后，才被告知可以离开，并得知他们的人力车已被留在勃伦南路（Brenan Road）附近的一块空地上。

获释后，他们前往那块空

pages.en:
- 5 -

ground but not finding their rickshas, came to Bubbling
Well Station to report the matter.

The rickshas taken from these pullers were those
found abandoned on Avenue Haig in the vicinity of the
shooting. They have been brought to Bubbling Well
Station by police and will later be handed over to the
owners.

A superficial examination of the car at the station
disclosed that it had been struck eight times by bullets.

The Finger Print Bureau were informed and took
photographs of the car which was later handed over to the
transport office for a further examination in conjunction
with the Officer in charge Arms Identification Section.
The two spent bullets found in the car at the station
were forwarded to Arms Identification Section.

Acting on the instructions of Mr. Conduit, D.D.C. "B"
further enquiries are being made by Chinese detectives in
the vicinity of the shooting.

For further particulars, please find attached
statements of Mr. Phillips' chauffeur, a newspaper
delivery coolie and three public ricksha coolies.

D.D.C. "B".

〔此处为手写签名〕
Det. Inspector.
pages.zh:

地，但未找到他们的人力车，于是来到静安寺捕房报告此事。

从这些车夫那里抢走的人力车正是在枪击现场附近的爱文义路上发现的那些被遗弃的车辆。警方已将这些车辆带回静安寺捕房，稍后将移交给车主。

在捕房对汽车进行的初步检查显示，车身共有八处弹痕。

指纹局接到通知并对汽车进行了拍照，随后汽车被移交给交通科，会同武器识别科主管进行进一步检查。
在站内汽车中发现的两枚废子弹已送交武器识别科。

根据“B”区副助理总监康杜伊特（Conduit）先生的指示，华籍侦探正在枪击现场附近进行进一步调查。

更多详情，请见附件中菲利普斯先生的司机、一名送报车夫和三名公共人力车夫的供词。

“B”区副助理总监。

〔此处为手写签名〕
探长。

pages.en:
Wong Ho Foo ( 王 合 福 )
Kempo D.S.I. Yeung
D'well 6-1-40 D.S.I. Chu Chi Huang

My name 's Wong Ho Foo, 44, Kempo, M/Ricksha coolie,
Pullers Lic. No. 3127, residing straw hut off Brenan Road.

At 6 a.m. 6-1-40, I engaged ricksha Lic. No. 8860 from
the Mei Fang Li, Robison Road.

I went to Brenan Road where I was engaged by a male
Chinese aged about 30, height about 5' 5", medium build,
long face, grey long gown, cropped hair, Anhwei dialect.

I was told to pull my passenger to the Yung Ching Li,
off Jessfield Road. On arrival I was told to go into an
alleyway opposite the Yung Ching Li and once inside another
ricksha came to the spot and the passenger of that ricksha
spoke to my passenger.

A few seconds later another ricksha came on the scene.
The passenger of this ricksha alighted and went along the
alleyway together with the passenger of the second ricksha,
whilst my passenger remained seated in the ricksha.

About five minutes later, the two other passengers
returned with five or six other male Chinese all armed with
Mauser pistols and told us to take off our blue pullers'
smocks and give them to them.

This we did and they also took a blue short jacket from
me. Two of the men then took us to a teashop in the lane.
They kept us there until about 9.30 a.m. when they told us
we could go and that we should find our rickshas on a piece
of vacant ground off Brenan Road. We three pullers went
there together but could not find the rickshas.

The two other pullers went to D'well Police Station to
pages.zh:
王合福 (Wong Ho Foo)
静安寺巡捕房 杨警佐
贝威尔巡捕房 1940年1月6日 朱志黄警佐

我叫王合福，44岁，籍贯江苏金浦（音译），职业为人力车夫，
车夫执照号码3127号，居住在勃伦路旁的一间草棚内。

1940年1月6日上午6时，我在罗宾森路梅芳里雇用了一辆牌照号为8860的人力车。

我拉车前往勃伦路，在那里被一名约30岁的中国男子雇用。该男子身高约5英尺5英寸，中等身材，长脸，身穿灰色长衫，短发，讲安徽话。

我奉命将乘客拉至杰斯菲尔德路旁的永庆里。到达后，我被指示进入永庆里对面的一条弄堂。刚进去不久，另一辆人力车也来到该处，那辆车的乘客与我的乘客交谈起来。

几秒钟后，又有一辆人力车来到现场。这辆车的乘客下车，与第二辆人力车的乘客一同沿弄堂走去，而我的乘客则仍坐在人力车上。

大约五分钟后，另外两名乘客带着五六名其他中国男子返回，这些人均持有毛瑟手枪，并命令我们脱下蓝色的车夫罩衫交给他们。

我们照做了，他们还从我这里拿走了一件蓝色短夹克。随后，其中两人将我们带到弄堂里的一家茶馆。他们将我们扣留在那里，直到上午9时30分左右，才告诉我们可以离开，并说我们应该在勃伦路旁的一块空地上找到我们的人力车。我们三名车夫一同前往那里，但未能找到人力车。

另外两名车夫前往贝威尔巡捕房去

pages.en:
report the matter and as they were leaving, a pedestrian told
me that the rickshas might be at the Route Say Zoong Police
Station, French Concession so I went there.
On arrival there I ask the policeman on the gate if our
rickshas were there and he allowed me to go inside to see if
they were in the compound. As they were not there, I came to
B'well Police Station to report.
This is my true statement.
Sgd. A thumb printed. Wong Ho Foo.
pages.zh:
报案，当他们离开时，一名行人告诉我，人力车可能在法租界萨佐翁路（Route Say Zoong）巡捕房，于是我便去了那里。
到达那里后，我问门口的警察我们的人力车是否在那里，他允许我进去看看是否在院子里。由于不在那里，我便来到贝威尔巡捕房报案。
这是我的真实陈述。
签名并按指印。王合福。

pages.en:
Chi Ta Hong (季志洪)
Kompo                                      D.S.I. Young
B'well           6-1-40                    D.S.I. Chu Chi Huang.

My name is Chi Ta Hong, 36, Kompo, M/Ricsha coolie,
residing straw hut off Brenan Road, Puller's i.i.c. No. 7688.
    At 5.45 a.m. 6-1-40, I hired a ricsha, Lic. No. 253 from
the Ts Hai Boo Ricsha Co. at Brenan Road. I pulled my
ricsha to near Brenan Piece when I was called by a male
Chinese about 30, height about 5' 5", slight build, blue
skirt, Anhwei dialect, to pull him to the Yung Ching Li,
Jessfield Road. When we arrived there, the passenger told
me to go into an alleyway on the opposite side of the road.
    When we arrived inside the alleyway, I saw another ricsha
and puller in the lane and almost simultaneous with my
arrival another ricsha came on the scene.
    My passenger and one of the others went along the lane
and returned a few minutes later with several other men,
all armed with large pistols. They told us they wanted to
borrow our ricshas and told us to take off our ricsha
pullers smocks. They also took an overcoat from me.
    Two of them then took us to a nearby teashop where they
kept us until after 2 a.m. when they told us we could go and
would find our ricshas on a piece of waste ground on Brenan
Road.
    We went there but as we could not find them, I came to
B'well Police Station to report the matter.
    This is my true statement.
                Sgd. a thumb printed. Chi Ta Hong.
pages.zh:
季志洪 (Chi Ta Hong)
金浦（音译）                                      杨警佐
贝威尔巡捕房           1940年1月6日                    朱志黄警佐。

我叫季志洪，36岁，籍贯金浦（音译），职业为人力车夫，
居住在勃伦路旁的一间草棚内，车夫身份证号码7688号。
    1940年1月6日上午5时45分，我从勃伦路的慈海宝（音译）人力车公司租用了一辆车牌号为253的人力车。当我拉车到勃伦路附近的勃伦片场（Brenan Piece，音译）时，一名约30岁的中国男子叫住了我。该男子身高约5英尺5英寸，身材瘦削，身穿蓝袍，讲安徽话，让我拉他去杰斯菲尔德路的永庆里。当我们到达那里时，乘客让我进入马路对面的一条弄堂。
    当我们进入弄堂后，我看到巷子里有另一辆人力车和车夫，几乎在我到达的同时，又有一辆人力车来到现场。
    我的乘客和另一名乘客中的一人沿弄堂走去，几分钟后带着另外几名男子返回，这些人均持有大号手枪。他们说想借用我们的人力车，并让我们脱下车夫罩衫。他们还从我这里拿走了一件大衣。
    随后，其中两人将我们带到附近的一家茶馆，将我们扣留在那里直到凌晨2点以后，然后告诉我们可以离开，并说我们会在勃伦路的一块荒地上找到我们的人力车。
    我们去那里寻找，但因未能找到，我便来到贝威尔巡捕房报案。
    这是我的真实陈述。
                签名并按指印。季志洪。

pages.en:
Zau Tseng Yei (曹振賢)
Kompo                                      D.S.I. Young
B'well           6-1-40                    D.S.I. Chu Chi Huang.

My name is Zau Tseng Yei, 38, Kompo, S/Ricksha coolie,
Puller's Lic. No. 12376, residing straw hut off Brenan Road.

At 5.45 a.m. 6-1-40, I engaged a ricksha Lic. No. 7578
from a hong on Robison Road. I went to Robison Road near
Brenan Road when a male Chinese aged about 30, height about
5' 4", medium build, long thin face, wearing black long gown,
no hat, Northern dialect, engaged me to pull him to Jessfield
Road. We entered an alleyway on Jessfield Road and just
inside the alleyway, I saw two other rickshas and their
pullers there. I was told to wait and my passenger and a
passenger of one of the other rickshas went along the lane
and about 5 minutes later returned with several others, all
armed with large pistols.

We were made to take off our ricksha pullers smocks and
they also took another short jacket from me.

Two of the men then took us to a teashop in a straw hut
nearby.

We were kept there until after 9 a.m. when we were allowed
to go, being told that we should find our rickshas on a piece
of waste ground off Brenan Road.

We went there together but as we could not find the
rickshas, I came to B'well Station to report the matter.

This is my true statement.

Sgd. A thumb printed. Zau Tseng Yei.
pages.zh:
曹振贤 (Zau Tseng Yei)
金浦（音译）                                      杨警佐
贝威尔巡捕房           1940年1月6日                    朱志黄警佐。

我叫曹振贤，38岁，籍贯金浦（音译），职业为人力车夫，
车夫执照号码12376号，居住在勃伦路旁的一间草棚内。

1940年1月6日上午5时45分，我从罗宾森路的一家商行租用了一辆车牌号为7578的人力车。我拉车到罗宾森路靠近勃伦路的地方，一名约30岁的中国男子雇用了我去杰斯菲尔德路。该男子身高约5英尺4英寸，中等身材，长瘦脸，身穿黑色长衫，未戴帽子，讲北方话。我们进入杰斯菲尔德路的一条弄堂，刚进弄堂口，我就看到那里还有另外两辆人力车及其车夫。我被告知等待，我的乘客和其中一辆人力车的乘客沿弄堂走去，大约5分钟后带着其他人返回，这些人均持有大号手枪。

我们被迫脱下车夫罩衫，他们还从我这里拿走了另一件短夹克。

随后，其中两人将我们带到附近一间草棚里的茶馆。

我们将被扣留在那里直到上午9点以后，才被允许离开，并被告知我们应该在勃伦路旁的一块荒地上找到我们的人力车。

我们一同前往那里，但因未能找到人力车，我便来到贝威尔巡捕房报案。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名并按指印。曹振贤。

pages.en:
Woo Ching Kuag （吴金根）
Shanghai                                      D.S.I. Burton
B'well            6-1-40                       C.D.S. 219.

My name is Woo Ching Kuag, age 43, native of Shanghai,
reside at 643 Markham Road. I am a chauffeur employed by Mr.
Godfrey Phillips, residing No. 633 Avenue Haig and drive his
motor car Lic. No. 4160, my permit No. is 1149.

At 7 a.m. 6-1-40, I reported for work at my master's
home, No. 633 Ave. Haig and at 8.45 a.m. I drove the car to
the front door of my master's house and he entered the rear
seat of the car and told me to drive to office. I drove out
of the grounds onto Ave. Haig and was proceeding from West to
East on Ave. Haig, when about 100 yards West of Route Ferguson
I saw two public rickshas stationary on the North side of the
road, one in front of the other and as I was almost abreast
of them, one of the ricksha's coolies ran with ricksha across
the front of my car to the South side of the road. I applied
my brakes and slowed up the car to avoid causing an accident
and as I slowed down the second ricksha was pushed onto my
left front bumper and mudguard, this caused me to bring the
car to a standstill whereupon the man who had pushed the
ricksha onto my car pulled a long pistol from the front of his
short jacket and fired 8 or 9 shots into the car, on the
shots being fired both my master and I dropped to the floor
of the car, when no more shots were fired I raised myself
from the floor of the car and I saw 2 men running East along
Ave. Haig and saw them run into an alleyway on the North side
of the road about 20 yards ahead of me, I then re started
the car swerved off the ricksha and drove quickly East, my
master told me to drive slower, but as the two men had
pages.zh:
吴金根 （Woo Ching Kuag）
上海                                      伯顿警佐
贝威尔巡捕房            1940年1月6日                       C.D.S. 219.

我叫吴金根，43岁，上海人，
居住在马克姆路643号。我是戈弗雷·菲利普斯（Godfrey Phillips）先生雇用的司机，菲利普斯先生居住在海格路633号，我驾驶他的汽车，车牌号为4160，我的驾驶证号码是1149。

1940年1月6日上午7时，我到雇主家海格路633号上班，上午8时45分，我将车开到雇主家门口，他进入汽车后座，吩咐我开车去办公室。我驶出大院进入海格路，由西向东行驶，当行至弗格森路（Route Ferguson）以西约100码处时，我看到路北停着两辆公共人力车，一前一后。当我几乎与它们并排时，其中一辆人力车的车夫拉着车跑过我的车头到了路南。我踩下刹车减速以避免发生事故，就在我减速时，第二辆人力车被推撞到我的左前保险杠和挡泥板上，这迫使我停车。随即，那个将人力车推到我车上的人从短夹克前襟掏出一支长管手枪，向车内开了8或9枪。枪响时，我和雇主都伏倒在车底板上。当不再开枪时，我从车底板抬起头，看到两名男子沿海格路向东奔跑，并看到他们跑进前方约20码处路北的一条弄堂。随后我重新发动汽车，避开人力车，迅速向东驶去。雇主叫我开慢点，但由于那两人已经

pages.en:
entered the alleyway ahead of me I wanted to get away from
the place, thinking they may fire at us again, my intention
being to report to the B'well Police Station. I did not see
what the man with the riosha who had crossed to the South
side of the road did, when the shooting started and as far
as I know only one man fired at the car. I cannot give any
description of the men but the man that did the shooting was
dressed in a dark blue jacket and had a dark blue apron
around his waist and wore a dark grey Chinese coolie hat
skull type. The shooting occurred about 5 minutes after we
had left for office making the time about 8.50 a.m. After
we hand left the scene of the shooting I drove to B'well
Station to report with my master's consent.
This is my true statement.
Teo Ching Kung.
pages.zh:
进入了前方的弄堂，我想尽快离开该地，担心他们可能再次向我们开枪，我的意图是前往贝威尔巡捕房报案。我没有看到那名跑到路南的人力车夫在枪战开始时做了什么，据我所知，只有一人向汽车开枪。我无法提供这些人的体貌特征描述，但开枪者身穿深蓝色夹克，腰间系着深蓝色围裙，头戴深灰色中式瓜皮帽。枪击发生在我们出发去办公室后约5分钟，即时间约为上午8时50分。离开枪击现场后，经雇主同意，我驾车前往贝威尔巡捕房报案。
这是我的真实陈述。
张清公（Teo Ching Kung，音译）。

pages.en:
Nga Wu Zang (顏和昌)
Soochow                                D.S&I. Gellobkoff
B'well            6-1-40                C.D.S. 142

My name is Nga Wu Zang, age 36, native of Soochow,
married, employed as a delivery coolie by Ts Wu Zang agent
distributing newspapers and I reside at my employer's house
No. 19 Ching Yih Lee, Rue Brenier de Montmorand.
    On the morning of 6-1-40 I was, as usually, delivering
newspapers to subscribers on Ave. Haig. At about 8.50 a.m.
even date, I was riding my bicycle, F.M.C. Lic. No. 2344
proceeding East along Ave. Haig near "Clove Gardens" when I
heard some noise behind me. I stopped my bicycle and on
looking about saw an East bound green coloured m/car collide
with a public ricksha. Another public ricksha was placed
across the road on the South side of Ave. Haig. The m/car
stopped and then a man wearing blue jacket and pants, who
was standing on the N. footpath, knelt down, produced a
Mauser pistol and fired several shots at the car. The car
proceeded East along Ave. Haig and the armed man ran after
it and continued to fire at the car. The m/car, however,
gained speed and disappeared. Then another man wearing dark
coloured old overcoat who had been standing near the public
rickshas on the South side of the road followed the armed man
and they ran past me in Easterly direction. There was a
third public ricksha parked on the North footpath about 20
yards in front of me and when the armed man and his accomplice
ran past it, the puller of the third ricksha left his vehicle,
joined the assassins and together with them escaped East
along Ave. Haig. At that time there was no one else on the
road and only the three empty rickshas remained abandoned.

我叫颜和昌，36岁，苏州人，
已婚，受雇于曾武藏（Ts Wu Zang，音译）代理商行担任送报苦力，我居住在蒙马朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）正义里19号雇主家中。
    1940年1月6日上午，我像往常一样在海格路向订户送报。当天上午约8时50分，我骑着自行车（法租界执照号码2344号）沿海格路向东行驶，经过“丁香花园”（Clove Gardens）附近时，听到身后传来一些噪音。我停下自行车，环顾四周，看到一辆向东行驶的绿色轿车与一辆公共人力车相撞。另一辆公共人力车横在海格路南侧的马路上。轿车停下后，一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的男子——他原站在北侧人行道上——跪下来，掏出一支毛瑟手枪，向轿车开了几枪。轿车沿海格路继续向东行驶，持枪男子追赶并向轿车持续射击。然而，轿车加速并消失了。随后，另一名身穿深色旧大衣的男子——他原站在路南的公共人力车附近——跟随持枪男子，他们从我身边跑过，向东而去。在我前方约20码处的北侧人行道上停着第三辆公共人力车，当持枪男子及其同伙跑过该车时，第三名车夫离开车辆，加入了刺客行列，与他们一起沿海格路向东逃窜。当时路上没有其他人，只剩下三辆空置的人力车被遗弃在现场。

pages.en:
A few minutes later, the Police arrived and I reported to a
Chinese Detective what I had seen. Then I was requested to
come to the B'well Station where I made this statement.
This is my true statement.
sgd. & thumb printed. Nga Wu Zang.

几分钟后，警察赶到，我向一名华探报告了我所见的情况。随后，我被要求来到贝威尔巡捕房，在此作了这份陈述。
这是我的真实陈述。
签名并按指印。颜和昌。

ATTEMPTED ASSASSINATION OF MR. GODFREY PHILLIPS,
SECRETARY GENERAL S.M.C.

At 8.30 a.m. Mr. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary
General S.M.C., was proceeding in his motor car, which
was driven by his own private chauffeur, East along
Avenue Haig and when about 200 yards West of Route
Ferguson a ricsha ran from the North side of the
road and collided with the car causing same to stop.
Another ricsha was stationary on the North side of
the road. Immediately the car stopped a number of
shots were fired at the car by the persons who had
been in charge of these ricshas. Eight bullets hit
the car, all on the left side, but no one was wounded.
The chauffeur immediately accelerated and the car, which
had only stopped for a fraction of a minute, proceeded
to B'well Police Station. Detectives were immediately
sent to the scene to investigate and C.D.S. 283 received
information from a male Chinese, who is known to him
as an employee of a gambling house in the vicinity,
that three men all armed with pistols had been arrested
by the agents of Wang Ching Wei and taken to the Sub-
Station situated at 21 Mei Hwa Li (美華里) Tsoo Ka Koh
(朱家庫). C.D.S. 283 reported this to a foreign detective
at the scene and at this time the informant disappeared.

C.I. MacFarlane immediately interviewed Supt. Wong
Tuh Ling (王德林) of the Shanghai City Government Police
Bureau and verified from him that three men had actually

At about 9.45 a.m. two ricsha coolies and
later another ricsha coolie, came into B'Well Station
and made the following report.

At about 5.45 a.m. their ricshas were hired
near Brennan Piece by three men who instructed them to
proceed to Yoong Ching Li (永慶里), Jessfield Road.
On arrival there, the three passengers produced pistols
and forced the coolies to exchange clothes with them,
and the three passengers then took away the ricshas,
whilst the three coolies were detained in a nearby
teashop by two other men.

At about 9.30 a.m. these three coolies were
told they could go and that they would find their
ricshas behind the teashop. As they could not find
them there, they reported the theft to B'Well Road
Station.

上午约9时30分，这三名车夫被告知可以离开，并称他们将在茶楼后面找到他们的人力车。由于他们在那里未能找到车辆，遂向静安寺路捕房报告失窃。

Later in the afternoon (about 3.45p.m.) Mr.Yorke

Fujino, Officer i/c of the Japanese Gendarmerie who
very brusquely stated that he had been asked on five
different occasions regarding the handing over of the
assassins and that as far as he knew there had been no
such arrests made by any of his men or agents.

assertion that the assassins had been arrested by his
men and the undersigned stated that he was not prepared
to produce this at the moment. With this the interview
ended and Major Fujino made a parting shot by adding
that if the S.M.Police thought that the S.C.G.Police had
the arrested men, they (the S.M.P.) had better go to

H. Q. C. B. Station,
Date January 22, 1940

Subject Further to statement of C.P.C. 1515 (B'Well).

Made by and Forwarded by C. D. I. Toon

CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,
.X.
Further to statement made by C.P.C. 1515
(B'Well) this C.P.C. stated that he had information
to the effect that the persons mentioned by him had
received an invitation from one named Zung Wa Ming
(陳華明), native of Anhwei, to a party he was giving
at the Bah Li Restaurant (白利 ), corner of
Edinburgh and Brenan Roads, on January 16, 1940.

Arrangements were accordingly made for
this C.P.C. to follow up his information and he reports
that Zung Kya Nyi (陳家義) was present at this party.

Further information was received by C.P.C.
1515 to the effect that these men may also visit the
Eventail Night Club, 1238 Yu Yuen Road, on January 19,
1940, on the occasion of the marriage of the daughter
of Chu Sung Ling (朱順林), notorious gambling den
conductor in the Western District.

C.P.C. 1515 reports also having seen Zung
Kya Nyi attending this function.

It will be recalled that Zung Kya Nyi was
the person seen dressed in ricsha coolies clothing,
pulling a ricsha, together with Ting Kyi Kuan (丁建坤)
(armed with a pistol) at about 6 a.m. January 6, 1940
in South Zau Ka Zah Village, this was the same morning
the attempt was made on Mr. Godfrey Phillips on Avenue
Haig.

D.C. (Crime)
C. D. I.

事由 关于静安寺捕房便衣警员1515号陈述的补充。

由刑事处侦探长 Toon 撰写并呈报

机密

先生，
.X.
继静安寺捕房便衣警员1515号所作陈述之后，该便衣警员称，他掌握情报，其所提及的人员收到了名为陈华明（Zung Wa Ming，安徽籍）的邀请，参加其于1940年1月16日在爱丁堡路与布伦南路拐角处的白利餐厅（Bah Li Restaurant）举办的聚会。

据此安排该便衣警员跟进其情报，他报告称陈家义（Zung Kya Nyi）出席了此次聚会。

便衣警员1515号又收到情报，称这些人也可能于1940年1月19日前往愚园路1238号的Eventail夜总会，参加西区著名赌窟经营者朱顺林（Chu Sung Ling）之女婚礼。

便衣警员1515号还报告称目睹陈家义出席该活动。

兹回顾，陈家义即是1940年1月6日上午约6时在曹家寨南村（South Zau Ka Zah Village）被人看见身穿人力车夫服装、拉着人力车，并与持枪的丁建坤（Ting Kyi Kuan）在一起的人，这正是Godfrey Phillips先生在爱文义路遇刺未遂案的同一早晨。

D.C. (刑事)
C. D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of C.P.C.1515, Sung Ching Daung (沈清堂)
native of Hofei, Anhwei taken by D.S.I. Fowler
at C.B.H.Q.(C.1) on the 9.1.40 and interpreted by D.S.I. Wu Chen Mao.

My name is Sung Ching Daung, 34, Hofei, Anhwei,
C.P.C. 1515 attached to Bubbling-Well Station and residing
at 611 Robison Road (O.O.L.).

In July 1939 I married (my second marriage) one named
Ting Zeu Ying (丁善英) native of Hofei, Anhwei. She had
a friend named Zee Dah Pan (徐大) also a native of Hofei,
Anhwei. This person was engaged in taking salted meat etc
from her village to Shanghai for sale. On several occasions on
her visiting Shanghai she has stayed at my home.

Through the brother of my former wife, Wong Nyih Kwei
(王業貴) 36, Anhwei, residing 38 South Zau Ka Zah off Jess-
field Road, who was formerly a weaver and later an armed guard
at one of the opium hongs in the Sing Kong Li off Jessfield
Road, I learned the following:-

He had been engaged as an armed guard by one Tsu Zung
Ling (朱順林) together with Ting Kyi Kuan (丁建坤), Zung Kya
Nyi (陳家義), Wong Kyi Keu (黃其寬), Doong Shing Kwei (董興貴)
who all lived together at 38 South Zau Ka Zah, Jessfield Road,
and about 20 others.

About May 1939 Tsu Zung Ling relinquished the position
of engaging guards and, as a result, Wong Nyih Kwei, Ting Kyi
Kuan, Zung Kya Nyi, Wong Kyi Keu, Doong Shing Kwei and a
number of others were thrown out of employment because they
did not know the new contractor.

About July or August, Ting Kyi Kuan, and Zung Kya Nyi
secured employment at the Foo Sung (富生) Gambling den at
Brenan Piece, as guards. None of the guards were armed.

警方调查报告。

以下为巡长 1515 号沈清堂（Sung Ching Daung，安徽合肥人）的陈述，
由副督察福勒于1940年1月9日在中央捕房总部（C.1）记录，
并由副督察吴振茂（Wu Chen Mao）翻译。

我叫沈清堂，34岁，安徽合肥人，
隶属于静安寺捕房的巡长 1515 号，
居住在罗别根路（Robison Road）611号（外侨名录地址）。

1939年7月，我娶了（第二次婚姻）一位名叫
丁善英（Ting Zeu Ying）的女子，她是安徽合肥人。她有一位
名叫徐大（Zee Dah Pan，音译）的朋友，也是安徽合肥人。此人从事
将咸肉等物品从其家乡运至上海出售的工作。她几次来上海时，
都住在我家。

通过我前妻的兄弟王业贵（Wong Nyih Kwei），36岁，安徽人，
居住在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）曹家宅（Zau Ka Zah）南38号，
他以前是织布工，后来在极司菲尔路新康里（Sing Kong Li）的一家
鸦片烟馆担任武装警卫，我得知了以下情况：

他被朱顺林（Tsu Zung Ling）雇佣为武装警卫，同被雇佣的还有
丁建坤（Ting Kyi Kuan）、陈家义（Zung Kya Nyi）、黄其宽（Wong Kyi Keu）、
董兴贵（Doong Shing Kwei），他们都一起住在极司菲尔路曹家宅南38号，
此外还有大约20其他人。

1939年5月左右，朱顺林不再负责雇佣警卫，因此，
王业贵、丁建坤、陈家义、黄其宽、董兴贵及其他一些人
因不认识新的承包商而失业。

大约在7月或8月，丁建坤和陈家义在贝伦片（Brenan Piece，音译）的
富生（Foo Sung）赌场找到了警卫的工作。这些警卫均未配备武器。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of ______________________________________________________
native of __________________________________ taken by me _______________________________
at ____________________ on the ____________________ and interpreted by __________________

- 2 -

About August my former brother-in-law Wong Nyih Kwei asked me my opinion re him joining the Wang Ching Wei clique. Whilst not giving any definite opinion I advised him not to do so. I learned that persons wishing to join the clique had to possess a pistol and this my former brother-in-law had not.

About the beginning of September I learned from my former brother-in-law, who was still unemployed, that Ting Kyi Kuan, Zung Kya Nyi and one other Wong Ah Hsiang (王阿香) had, after purchasing pistols, joined the Wang Ching Wei clique and were posted at 12 Yoong Loh Tsung (永樂邨) (Lane 759) Jessfield Road.

I thereafter saw Zung Kya Nyi and Wong Ah Hsiang dressed smartly in civilian clothing.

On or about December 23rd or 24th, I learned from my former brother-in-law that Ting Kyi Kuan, who had become a group leader, Zung Kya Nyi and Wong Ah Hsiang and several others had, on September 16, 1939, robbed the service pistols from C.P.C.s 2125 and 2810 on Edinburgh near Brenan Roads.

Because I could not confirm the information and further more the persons allegedly concerned were residing in Japanese-occupied territory, I did not report to any S.M.Police Officer.

On the morning of January 4, 1940, Zee Dah Pan, the friend of my present wife, came to my home, She had arrived from Hofei, Anhwei two or three days previously to sell salted meat etc. She stayed at my home on the night of the 4th.

On the morning of the 5th I asked her to try and sleep

C.D.I. Nakamura

Sir,

    In accordance with instructions from D.C.
(Crime) to negotiate with Major Hayashi of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Headquarters for the loan of three suspects,
who were reported to have been arrested by the Chinese
Authorities in the Western District for having attempted
to assassinate Mr. G. Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner
General, on Avenue Haig on the morning of January 6,
1940, I requested Major Hayashi over telephone at 1 p.m.
January 6 for the loan and was informed by him that as
he had just returned from Nantao and had received no
information regarding the case he would make enquiries
and do his best to have the arrested persons if any
to be loaned to us.

    At 5 p.m. on the same date on behalf of Lt.
Toita, personal assistant to Major Hayashi informed
me by telephone that no suspects had been arrested
either by the Gendarmerie or by the Chinese Police
in the Western District.

    He further asked me the source of such
information to which I replied that according to
reliable information obtained the suspects had escaped
into the Sun Sun Club (新々), situated in the
vicinity of the scene of crime, where they were arrested
and taken to No. 76 Jessfield Road.

    He told me that further enquiries would be
made and that results would be communicated to us later.

ATTEMPTED ASSASSINATION OF MR. GODFREY
PHILLIPS, SECRETARY GENERAL, S.M.C.

At about 8.50 a.m. on 61.40, Mr. Godfrey
Phillips, Secretary General S.M.C., was proceeding
East along Avenue Haig in his motor-car, which was
driven by his private chauffeur, and when about 100
yards West of Route Ferguson at a point immediately
outside the Clove Garden Amusement Resort, one of
two public ricshas which were waiting on the North
side of the road, dashed across the road in front
of the oncoming car. This caused the car to slow
down and then the other ricsha was pushed by the
puller into the back mudguard and bumper of the
car, and this caused the chauffeur to bring the
car to a standstill. The puller of the second
ricsha was seen to pull out a Mauser from beneath
his jacket and open fire. A number of shots were
fired, eight of which hit the motor car on the left
side and the Arms Identification Section later dis-
covered that at least three pistols were used. Neither
Mr. Phillips or the chauffeur was wounded and on Mr.

Commanding Japanese Gendarmerie,Shanghai.
To : Major-General F.K. Simmons,
Commanding British Defence Force, Shanghai.
Sir, 8th January, 1940.
I have the honour to acknowledge your letter of the 6th
January requesting the handing over of criminals.
At the present time when negotiations regarding the policing
of the Western Extension area are proceeding smoothly between the
Municipal Council and the Shanghai Special City Government I am
aghast at the direct action taken against Mr. Phillips, the
Commissioner General of the Municipal Council and filled with the
deepest regret at this most contemptible deed.
On receipt of your letter and the very rapid report from the
Municipal Police almost immediately after the incident occurred
I at once made investigations and found that there was no truth in
the statement that the criminals were being detained at the Western
District Detachment of the Gendarmerie; furthermore the investiga-
tion conducted by the Special City Government Police have up to date
also failed to establish any truth in the statement. I am astonished
that this (allegation) was made and as regards the source of the
information, I have a grave suspicion that it must be due to some
misunderstanding or to the machinations of ill-disposed persons.
However, in view of the grave nature of this occurrence,
I am urging on my subordinates and the City Government Police and
doing my best to effect the arrest of the criminals. Should they
be arrested I shall give very special consideration to the question
of complying with your wishes and I hope that I may look for your
continued cooperation in the future.
The foregoing is my very hurried reply.
I have etc.

收到阁下来信以及事发后几乎立即从市警察局收到的迅速报告后，我立即进行了调查，发现所谓罪犯被拘押在宪兵队西区分队之说并无事实依据；此外，特别市政府警察进行的调查迄今也未能证实该说法属实。我对提出这种（指控）感到惊讶，至于信息来源，我严重怀疑这一定是由于某种误解或居心不良者的阴谋所致。

Translation of letter to Secretary and
Commissioner-General from the "Whole
Body of Loyal Chinese Constables."

Dated 11th January, 1940.

Mr. G. G. Phillips: Attack on

How horrified and dismayed were we when we learned of the
incident that befell you according to press reports, and how
concerned did we feel for your safety! We prayed fervently to
God to protect our Superior Officer, Mr. Phillips; happily,
our prayer was answered and you are now safe; the importance
of your position as Commissioner-General is thus all the more
clearly demonstrated. The wicked design of bad characters has
been defeated; we only have to deplore that you, our dear
Mr. Phillips, have been given a fright.

It is rather an honour than a disgrace, to be deemed worthy
of being plotted against by the evil elements. The righteous
and the evil can never unite; good and evil cannot stand together
as light and darkness are fundamentally opposed to each another.

The threat to your safety was merely a preliminary step
to threatening the security of the several millions of residents
in this city which number more than the population of a small
nation. The Council's highest Executive, in fact the Council
itself, has been conspired against by bad characters. This is
tantamount to striking a fated blow at the prestige of the
various Powers that have signed treaties with the Chinese
Government. Their shooting at our Commissioner-General is the
same thing as shooting at us. You have suffered this shock
because you were unwilling to compromise with or give way to the
forces of evil. We, indeed all residents in this city, and all
who love righteousness in the whole world, sympathize with you
and are highly incensed. We hope that no weakness will be shown

“全体忠诚华籍巡捕”致秘书兼总办的信函译文。

日期：1940年1月11日。

G. G. Phillips 先生：袭击事件

当我们从报纸报道中得知发生在您身上的事件时，我们是多么惊恐和沮丧，又是多么为您的安全担忧！我们 fervently（虔诚地）向上帝祈祷，保佑我们的上级长官 Phillips 先生；幸而，我们的祈祷得到了回应，您现在安然无恙；这也更加清楚地证明了您作为总办职位的重要性。坏人的邪恶图谋已被挫败；我们只痛惜亲爱的 Phillips 先生您受到了惊吓。

被邪恶势力视为值得策划攻击的对象，与其说是耻辱，不如说是荣耀。正邪不能共存；善恶不能并立，正如光与暗根本对立一样。

对您安全的威胁，仅仅是威胁这座拥有数百万居民（超过一个小国的人口）的城市安全的前奏。工部局的最高行政长官，事实上是整个工部局，都遭到了坏人的阴谋算计。这无异于对与中国政府签订条约的各列强威望给予致命一击。他们向我们总办开枪，就等于向我们开枪。您遭受此次冲击，是因为您不愿与邪恶势力妥协或让步。我们，乃至本市所有居民，以及全世界所有热爱正义的人士，都同情您并深感愤慨。我们希望不要表现出

pages.en:
Translator's notes and comments.

(1) It would seem that the avowed fervent praying must
have taken place, if at all, before the episode happened,
for after the happening there could scarcely be any
logical need to invoke Deity for a dispensation already
vouchsafed.

(2) It is assumed that the wicked design of bad characters,
though defeated, at least succeeded in giving a fright.

(3) The "honour" referred to is something to take pride in,
and should not be overlooked. That ought to be ample
consolation, and justification to let the matter drop.

(4) The wicked design in all its iniquity was to strike
the Council and the Powers a fatal blow by ultimately
threatening the security of millions of residents. The
writer seems to be quite au fait with the purpose of the
vile plot, but does not appear to possess a very clear
conception as to the why and wherefore.

This rambling anonymous effusion obviously emanates from
the same source as the numerous indictments of the "empty-stomach"
gang, and its purpose is plainly twofold, (1) to trail another
red-herring across the track, and (2) to reinforce previous
demands. The fact that the letter bears no authentic signature,
and gives no definite address, makes it anonymous. A "Whole Body"
does not act in this way.

There seems to be some scope here for investigation, and
the handwriting and stationery, both very distinctive, might give
a clue if compared with previous letters received. I have a
faint recollection that there is a similar production in the
"Rice" file, which may give name and address; though most of those
letters had unreliable signatures.

The place of posting in each case can be traced. Yu Yuen
pages.zh:
译者注及评论。

(1) 看来，所谓的热切祈祷即便确实发生过，也必然是在该事件发生之前；因为在事件发生之后，几乎没有任何逻辑上的必要去祈求神明赐予一项已经恩准的豁免。

(2) 据推测，坏人的邪恶图谋虽然被挫败，但至少成功造成了惊吓。

(3) 此处提及的“荣誉”是一种值得自豪的事物，不应被忽视。这应当足以作为安慰，并为不再追究此事提供正当理由。

(4) 这一邪恶图谋的全部罪恶之处，在于最终通过威胁数百万居民的安全，给工部局和列强以致命打击。写信人似乎对该卑鄙阴谋的目的十分内行（au fait），但对于其前因后果似乎并没有非常清晰的概念。

这篇语无伦次的匿名文章显然与众多指控“空肚帮”的文章出自同一来源，其目的明显具有双重性：(1) 转移视线，制造干扰；(2) 强化先前的要求。由于信件没有真实的签名，也未提供确切的地址，因此属于匿名信。“全体”（Whole Body）是不会以这种方式行事的。

此处似乎有一些调查的空间，其笔迹和信纸都非常独特，如果与此前收到的信件进行比对，可能会提供线索。我隐约记得在“米案”卷宗里有一份类似的文件，其中可能载有姓名和地址；尽管那些信件中的签名大多不可靠。

每封信的寄出地点均可追溯。余元（音译）

Dated 8th September, 1939.

Police: Do Chinese Constables receive temporary
allowance?

The prices of various commodities have recently reached
excessive heights, especially in the case of rice. It is
very difficult for a man drawing a salary of forty or fifty
dollars to support his family; the hardships being experienced
by those receiving still lower pay can be easily imagined.
The Council has done its utmost to stabilize the living
conditions of its employés in order that their working
efficiency may not be impaired by pecuniary worries, hence
the issue of the temporary allowance. We desire to be
informed whether or not the allowance is also granted to
Chinese detectives and constables whose pay is below forty
or fifty dollars, as they should not have to carry out their
duties on empty stomachs. There should be no impressions
of unfairness in the mind of the public. If they do not
receive the allowance, we beg the Council to accord them
equal treatment so that their efficiency, on which the safety
of ratepayers rests, may be maintained.

(Chopped) Chinese Ratepayers' Association.

日期：1939年9月8日。

警务处：中国巡捕是否领取临时津贴？

近期各类商品价格涨至过高水平，尤其是大米。对于月薪四五十元的人来说，养家糊口非常困难；而那些薪水更低的人所经历的艰辛则不难想象。工部局已竭尽全力稳定雇员的生活条件，以免其工作效率因经济忧虑而受损，因此发放了临时津贴。我们希望获悉，月薪低于四五十元的中国侦探和巡捕是否也享有此津贴，因为他们不应空腹执勤。公众心中不应产生不公平的印象。如果他们未获得该津贴，我们恳请工部局给予他们同等待遇，以便维持其效率，而纳税人的安全正系于此。

（盖章）华人纳税会。

（注：1939年9月11日下午晚些时候收到以待翻译）。

C. Klien
（印：上海公共租界工部局 1939年9月11日）

CONFIDENTIAL

Translation of letter to Secretary-
General G.G. Phillips, Shanghai Municipal
Council, from the Shanghai Branch, Chinese
Traitors Extermination Corps.

Dated, January 18, 1940.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 22 JAN. 1940 / SECRETARY'S OFFICE）

Dear Mr. Phillips,

Some time ago we read in the paper that bad characters
attacked you but failed. We were very glad of the news. The
several bad characters arrested were actually kept by a certain
party. We are disgusted with this affair. Recently we have sent
out men to make a thorough enquiry. The following is the information
we gathered.
永 樂 
Formerly at House 12, Yun Loh Tsung (Ever Happy Alleyway),
Jessfield Road, was the office of the so-called West Shanghai Special
Service Section or the Plain Clothes Investigation Section, with
over 20 members under Mr. Ting. They have several pieces of new
modern weapons. They are all lawless elements and doing the work
of extortion, murder and kidnapping. They are frequently employed
by a certain party to disturb the peace and order and to attack
and assassinate whoever is hated by a certain party and to be got
rid of, either induced by money payment or ordered by threat of
force. This time the attempted assassination on you was actually
done by members of this section dressed like riosha coolies. They
attempted to put you to death but they failed to achieve their
purpose. Therefore their office has been moved to an alleyway just
opposite the Ever Happy Alleyway. Their new address is at Houses
信 義 
25-27, Sing Nee Tsung (Honest and Righteous Alleyway), Jessfield Road.

If this group is not dissolved and severely punished your
life will remain in danger. It is afraid that you might repent for
it in future. We are very worried about this serious problem and
therefore respectfully report the true facts to you and request you
to immediately despatch people to investigate in order to arrest
the whole group for investigation and punishment in order to
eliminate the source of danger. Whatever we know later we will
report again.

We wish you good health.

上海锄奸团上海分团致上海公共租界工部局秘书长 G.G. Phillips 的信函译文。

日期：1940年1月18日。
（印：上海公共租界工部局 / 1940年1月22日 / 秘书处办公室）

尊敬的 Phillips 先生：

前几日我们在报纸上读到坏人袭击您但未遂的消息。我们对此消息感到非常高兴。被捕的几个坏人实际上是被某一方包庇的。我们对这件事感到厌恶。最近我们派人进行了彻底调查。以下是我们收集到的信息。
永 樂 
以前位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）永乐弄12号的，是所谓的“西上海特别服务组”或“便衣调查组”的办公室，在丁先生手下有20多名成员。他们拥有几件新的现代武器。他们均为不法之徒，从事勒索、谋杀和绑架活动。他们经常受某一方雇佣，扰乱治安秩序，并攻击和暗杀某一方所憎恨且欲除之而后快的人，手段或是金钱利诱，或是武力威胁。此次对您实施的未遂暗杀，实际上是由该组伪装成俄罗斯苦力（riosha coolies）的成员所为。他们企图置您于死地，但未能得逞。因此，他们的办公室已搬至紧邻永乐弄对面的一条弄堂。他们的新地址是极司菲尔路信义弄25-27号。
信 義 

如果不解散该团伙并予以严惩，您的生命仍将处于危险之中。恐怕您将来会为此后悔。我们非常担心这一严重问题，因此特此向您如实报告，并请求您立即派人调查，以便逮捕整个团伙进行调查和惩处，从而消除危险源头。日后如有所知，我们将再次报告。

祝您身体健康。
